Action.description:
A write the assistant made, as the turn reports it (I5: every direct write is reported
with its consequences).

consequences.description: What it newly caused in each journey it changed (D7).

nodes.description:
The nodes it wrote, in key order (I5: a direct change is reported with the nodes
it affected, which the panel links to); none for a write to no journey's nodes.

oneOf.description: Drafted as a proposal for the user to review and apply.
An open proposal discarded, at the assistant's hand.

Actor.description: Who made a change (H2): a user, or an agent acting for one.

agent.description: The agent acting for the user, if any.

AffectedNodes.description:
Some nodes an answer's effect names: how many in all, and the first
`explanation_entry_count_max` of them in tree order.

nodes.description: The first of them, in tree order, at most `explanation_entry_count_max`.

total.description: How many nodes there are in all.

AgentId.description: Starts with "ag_"; at most id_bytes_max (64) bytes.

AgentToken.description: An agent token as its user's list shows it: never the secret.

agent.description: The agent the token acts as.

revoked_at.description: When it was revoked, if it was.

Annotation.description:
A journey-authored note or link on a node or on the journey itself (G1), attributed and
timestamped from the patch that added it.

edited_at.description: When it was last edited, if ever.

AnnotationBody.description: A note or link as its author writes it (G1): the part an add or edit carries.

AnswerEffects.description:
C12, E3: what answering a decision does, per choice, and the static lines every answer
of a date or entity decision carries.

applies.description:
Whether the decision's answer is in effect: it is relevant, and not skipped. When not,
no answer changes any other node's relevance and every choice's effect is empty.

choices.description:
One entry per choice of a boolean, single-choice, or multi-choice decision, in the
decision's order (`false` before `true`); none for the other answer types.

fills_role.description: The role its answer fills (E3), for an entity or entity-list decision.

pins.description: The milestone its answer pins (E3), for a date decision.

AnswerText.description:
A text answer: any text up to the body limit, empty included (an empty submission is an
answer).

AnswerValue.description:
A decision's submitted answer (A4; PRD glossary, Answer). Submitted empty text or an
empty list is answered.

AssistantRequest.description:
`POST /api/journeys/{id}/assistant` and `POST /api/routes/{id}/draft/assistant`: one message of
the caller's conversation about that journey or draft.

AttachmentKey.description: Starts with "a_"; at most id_bytes_max (64) bytes.

AuthKind.description: The kinds of sign-in a host can offer.

oneOf.description: A static token or named dev user (H1).
OAuth or OIDC against a registered provider.
The built-in OAuth server for MCP clients (I2).
Google Cloud Identity-Aware Proxy's signed assertion.
The browser host's single local identity.

kind.description: What kind of provider it is.

Because.description: Why a write became a proposal.

oneOf.description: It changes structure, or writes a route or its draft (PRD glossary, Structural change).
It touches more nodes than one direct write may (I5).

count.description: The nodes it writes; absent when it may write every node of its domain.

oneOf.description:
It would carry the nodes the turn's direct writes touch past the limit one change
may (I5): with every later such write in the turn, one proposal.

count.description: The nodes the turn's direct writes and this one would touch together.

oneOf.description: The assistant drafted it as a proposal itself.

Blocker.description: A dependency that blocks a node (D1, Gating: Blocked).

Bound.description: A derived date bound and the chain that produced it (F3, F7).

chain.description: The chain from a pin, actual, or today that produced it.

Bypass.description:
A guard bypass as stored (D4): the guards bypassed, why, and the specific failures
present when it was applied.

failures.description: The failures present when the bypass was applied.

Capabilities.description: The capabilities document (`GET /api/capabilities`): what this host offers.

assistant.description: Whether the in-app assistant is available (I5).

auth.description: How people sign in, in the order the host asks.

mcp.description: Whether the host serves MCP at `/api/mcp` (I2).

sse.description: Whether the host streams revision ticks over SSE (H6).

Chain.description: A chain of constraints, with the dates fixed on it.

constraints.description: The constraints, in order along the chain.

fixed.description: The pins and actuals on it.

ChainList.description:
The contradictory chains a rejection lists (F5): at most
`chain_count_per_rejection_max`, and whether there were more.

chains.description: The chains found, up to the limit.

more.description: The search was cut short at the limit.

ChildEntry.description: One child in a node's detail.

display_state.description: D8: the state every surface shows for it.

Choice.description:
One choice of a single- or multi-choice decision: an id that answers and conditions use,
and an optional label. Written as the bare id when it has no label.

ChoiceEffect.description:
C12: what one answer to a decision does to the journey's scope, from a three-valued
re-evaluation of relevance under that answer: never a full derive.

answer.description:
The whole answer evaluated: a boolean, a choice, or (for a multi choice) the current
answer with `choice` toggled.

choice.description: The choice id, for a single or multi choice.

current.description:
This is the recorded answer (for a multi choice: `choice` is in it, so the answer
evaluated removes it).

decided_later.description:
Nodes that would stay undecided because they hang on another decision still to be
answered, which this answer opens or leaves open.

drops.description:
Nodes the answer settles as not relevant. Nodes that would still hang on another
unanswered decision are `decided_later`, never here.

drops_with_progress.description:
Of the drops, the nodes with recorded progress (started, done, decided, reached):
the answer does not undo it.

opens_decisions.description: Of those, the decisions that open: relevant and still to be answered.

Clause.description: A condition clause. The parser also holds the whole tree to 8 levels and 16 clauses, which JSON Schema cannot express.

oneOf.description: The answer does not equal the value.
The answer is one of the values.
The answer (a list, or text) contains the value.

ClauseResolved.description: A condition clause. The parser also holds the whole tree to 8 levels and 16 clauses, which JSON Schema cannot express.

oneOf.description: The answer does not equal the value.
The answer is one of the values.
The answer (a list, or text) contains the value.

decision.description: The decision whose answer is compared.

value.description: The value it is compared with.

decision.description: The decision whose answer is compared.

value.description: The value it is compared with.

Condition.description:
A `relevant_when` condition: a clause tree within `condition_depth_max` and
`condition_clause_count_max`, where clauses are the leaf predicates.

oneOf.description: The answer does not equal the value.
The answer is one of the values.
The answer (a list, or text) contains the value.

ConditionResolved.description:
A `relevant_when` condition: a clause tree within `condition_depth_max` and
`condition_clause_count_max`, where clauses are the leaf predicates.

oneOf.description: The answer does not equal the value.
The answer is one of the values.
The answer (a list, or text) contains the value.

ConditionText.description: A compared value: a choice id, date, entity key, or text; at most body_bytes_max bytes.

anyOf.description: Every other answer type, as text.

ConditionValue.description:
The value a clause compares an answer with: a boolean, or text that the decision's
answer type gives meaning (a choice id, a date, an entity key, or plain text).

Conflict.description:
What a conflict is about, with the journey's side and the route's (B7, B9). A side that
is absent is `None` (an absent edge is `false`).

oneOf.description: A node field the journey edited and the route changed to something else.

dangling.description:
The route's value names a node the journey does not hold, so it cannot be taken
(B4: a removed node's tombstone covers its subtree); only the journey's side is
offered.

oneOf.description: An explicit edge the journey added or removed, and the route the other way.
A participation the journey edited and the route changed to something else.
A resource the journey edited and the route changed to something else.

dangling.description:
The route's value names a node the journey does not hold, so it cannot be taken
(B4: a removed node's tombstone covers its subtree); only the journey's side is
offered.

oneOf.description:
A node whose kind or answer type differs while the journey edited its shape or holds
state the change would invalidate: the whole node is in conflict.

answered.description: The journey has answered it, so taking an answer-type change reopens it.

dangling.description:
The route's value names a node the journey does not hold, so it cannot be taken
(B4: a removed node's tombstone covers its subtree); only the journey's side is
offered.

oneOf.description: A decided decision whose answer names choices the route's choices no longer have.

rationale.description:
The rationale the journey's answer was given with, kept when the answer is
mapped onto the route's choices (B2).

oneOf.description:
A role both sides changed, one whose new cardinality cannot hold the journey's direct
fill, or one the route removed that the journey still refers to.

insertions.description:
The insertions that map a segment role onto it, when the route removed it (B13):
the role can then be kept or removed, not remapped.

members.description:
Who fills the role now (E3), when insertions map onto it: removing it hands
these to the segment's nodes directly.

references.description: What in the journey refers to it.

route.description: The route's role, none when it removed it.

oneOf.description:
A participation kind both sides changed, or one the route removed that the journey
still uses.

insertions.description:
The insertions that map a segment kind onto it, when the route removed it (B13):
the kind can then be kept or removed, not remapped.

references.description: The journey's participations of the kind, by node.

route.description: The route's kind, none when it removed it.

oneOf.description: The graph's `default_owner`, which both sides changed.

ConflictResolution.description:
How a reviewer resolves a conflict (B7, B9). Which resolutions a conflict offers depends
on what it is about ([`Conflict::offers`]); each becomes ordinary mutations when the
proposal is resolved.

oneOf.description: Keep the journey's value as a local edit, or its definition as an override.

Take the route's choices and map each removed choice the answer names to one that
remains (B7: map old to new).
Take the route's value and clear the state it makes invalid.
Take the route's value and reopen the node.

Point every reference to a role the route removed at another role, then remove it.
Not offered while an insertion maps a segment role onto it (B13).

role.description: The role the references move to.

oneOf.description:
Move every participation of a kind the route removed to another kind, then remove it.
Not offered while an insertion maps a segment kind onto it (B13).

kind.description: The kind the participations move to.

oneOf.description:
Clear every reference to a role or kind the route removed, then remove it. Where an
insertion maps a segment role onto a removed role, the segment's nodes keep what the
role held: whoever filled it now fills their participations directly, and the
insertion's mapping goes with the role (B13).

Consequences.description:
What an accepted patch or a proposal preview newly caused in derived state (D7),
reported with the result and never stored.

into_scope.description:
Informational: nodes that were not relevant and are now relevant or undecided, in key
order.

out_of_scope.description: Informational: nodes that were in scope and are now not relevant, in key order.

stale.description: Nodes that became stale or gained a stale reason.

undecided.description: Finished nodes newly undecided, which may not apply: a warning, never a rejection.

unlocked.description:
Informational, never a warning: nodes newly on the acting frontier, in key order. A
node the write adds is not unlocked by it.

Constraint.description:
One constraint: `after` is at least `offset_days` after `before` (offsets may be zero or
negative).

conditional.description: It passes through an undecided node, so it may not apply (F2).

offset_days.description: The least number of days between them.

ConstraintSource.description: Where a constraint comes from (F2): what to edit to change it (F7).

oneOf.description: A dependency: the dependent starts after the requirement finishes.
An estimate: a node finishes at least its estimate after it starts.
Containment: a child finishes before its parent's own work starts.
A stage's closing milestone bounding the group's finish (F4).

Contribution.description: A gravity or unlocks contribution: the node and how much it adds.

other_owner.description: It is owned by someone other than the node's owner (the owner factor of unlocks).

Conversation.description:
`GET /api/journeys/{id}/assistant` and `GET /api/routes/{id}/draft/assistant`: the caller's
conversation about that journey or draft (I5: one per target per user), as kept: its
newest messages, oldest first. A conversation not started yet has none.

conversation.description: The conversation's id, which every turn about this target answers too.

oneOf.description: Cairn, reporting a write the assistant made or how a turn ended.

ConversationEntry.description: One kept message of a conversation.

ConversationId.description: Starts with "cv_"; at most id_bytes_max (64) bytes.

Cursor.description:
A position in a projection's order: where the next page starts (I3, J4). Valid for the
same journey revision and derive inputs; a page read at another revision starts over.

DateOrigin.description:
Where a milestone's effective date comes from (F1, F7: pin, actual, and derived dates are
told apart).

oneOf.description: Its pin, set directly or by answering its feeding decision (E3).

DateRule.description:
A date rule (A8): `{before|after: <source(s)>, offset: <days>}`. Several sources are
several constraints; the offset defaults to 0.

DateRule2.description:
A date rule (A8): `{before|after: <source(s)>, offset: <days>}`. Several sources are
several constraints; the offset defaults to 0.

DecisionEntry.description: C12: one decision in the decision view: its answer and which nodes the answer affects.

affects.description: The nodes whose relevance a condition reading it decides, their descendants included.

answer.description: Its answer, while in effect (decided and in scope, E3).

display_state.description: D8: the state every surface shows for it.

hidden_prerequisites.description: Its unsatisfied prerequisites that no drawn edge stands for (C2's marker).

rationale.description: The rationale its answer was given with, while the answer is in effect (B2, C12).

DecisionView.description:
C12: the graph filtered to decisions and their gating edges, with answers and what each
answer affected. A projection of the level with only decisions shown, not a separate
structure.

DependencyVia.description: How a dependency arose (PRD glossary, Condition gate / implicit edge).

oneOf.description: A parent waiting on its child (Containment).

condition_on.description: The node whose condition creates the gate.

Deployment.description: The deployment domain (E6; ARCHITECTURE, Engine > Model: `Deployment`).

aliases.description:
Merged entities' old keys, each resolving to the entity it was merged into (E6), at
most `alias_count_per_entity_max` resolving to one entity.

revision.description: The deployment revision (H5).

DeriveInputs.description:
The inputs derive takes besides the journey (ARCHITECTURE, Terms: Derive inputs),
supplied by the host and never read by the engine.

deployment.description: The deployment context: entities, emails, and aliases at a revision (E4, E6).

today.description: Today, in the deployment's time zone.

viewer.description: The viewer's entities, resolved from verified emails (H3); usually one.

frontier.description: The frontier, ranked (Priority: ties by slack, gravity, key).

today.description: The today it was derived for.

DisplayState.description:
D8: the one state every surface shows for a node, composed from relevance, stored state,
effective skip, auto-reach, blocking and snooze, and from the D3 flags, which it leaves in
place. Stored state is what transitions act on; this is what people and agents read. The
first matching value in this order wins: `not_relevant`, `skipped`, `done`, `snoozed`,
`active`, `conditional`, `blocked`, `scheduled`, `ready`.

oneOf.description:
Nothing is in the way and nothing has started: actionable work, a container waiting
only on its own children with nothing started, or one ready to finish.

Started: stored `active`, or a container whose children are the only thing it waits
on and some work beneath it has started.

In scope and unfinished, and its own or an inherited gate is unsatisfied. A container
is never blocked by its own children.

It may apply: relevance is `undecided` and it is unfinished, or relevance is
`not_relevant` but pending on an undecided decision (`pending_on`).
An `auto_reach` milestone, unblocked, whose date is ahead.
`done`, `decided`, `reached`, auto-reached, or a group that satisfies dependencies.
Does not apply, and settled (Gating): the recorded state survives beneath it.
The deployment: its entities and aliases.

DomainDocument.description:
The domain document (ARCHITECTURE, Terms): a journey's graph and state, the inputs to
derive it, and the engine version. Nothing derived is in it; proposals are not part of it.

DraftSource.description: Where a route draft comes from (A11, A13, B8).

oneOf.description: Editing the latest published version (or an empty route).
Importing a route file; the import's content follows as ordinary mutations.
Saving a journey as a route (B8); its structure follows as ordinary mutations.

Edge.description:
An explicit `requires` edge (A3), identified by its two ends: `node` requires `requires`.
The graph document holds edges on the dependent node's `requires` list; changes and
removals name them this way.

EdgeEnd.description: One end of an edge an insertion adds: a node of the segment, or of the graph.

oneOf.description: A node by its key in the segment version.
A node by its key in the graph.

EdgeOrigin.description: C2: how an edge on the canvas arose (C1: implicit gates are drawn dotted).

oneOf.description: A condition gate: the dependent's condition reads the decision (Gating).

EffectiveDate.description:
A milestone's effective date (F1): its actual date if reached, else its pin, else its
derived due. What other constraints see when they reference it.

EffectiveParticipation.description: A node's effective participation of one kind (E2).

Email.description: An email address, at most email_bytes_max (254) bytes; stored trimmed and lower-cased (H3).

Ended.description: How a turn ended. The writes before any ending stand and are reported.

oneOf.description: The provider did not answer within `assistant_provider_call` (120 s).
The provider answered with an error.
The model was still calling tools after `assistant_tool_loop_iterations` (32) calls.

Entity.description: A person or team journeys refer to (PRD glossary, Entity), deployment-scoped.

emails.description:
Its emails, each held by at most one entity (H3), at most
`email_count_per_entity_max`. A merge joins two entities' emails, so the engine checks
the joined set too.

EntityKey.description: Starts with "e_"; at most id_bytes_max (64) bytes.

Event.description:
An append-only audit record of one mutation (J1). The delta is the after-state of every
record the mutation wrote or removed, in order, so replay applies it with nothing
re-derived; events never hold derived values.

confirming_user.description: Who confirmed it, when a proposal was applied (H2).

log.description:
The log it belongs to: its patch's domain, except a journey's deletion, which the
deployment log keeps (A19).

ordinal.description: Its position in the patch, from 0.

patch_id.description: The patch it came from; a patch's events share it.

EventPage.description: A page of events; `next` is where the next page starts, absent on the last.

next.description: Pass as `after` for the next page.

EventType.description:
An event's type (J1's list). Most mutations have one type; a few take theirs from
their content ([`Mutation::event_type`]).

Explained.description:
A list of explanation entries with its total (ARCHITECTURE, Read path): complete inside
the engine and the browser; a server response keeps the largest entries up to
`explanation_entry_count_max` and the total.

total.description: How many there are in all.

ExplainedField.description: ARCHITECTURE, Read path: a derived value whose explanation list a server response pages.

oneOf.description: The nodes that make up its gravity.
The nodes completing it would unblock.
The direct dependents completing it would not yet free, with what else each waits on.

ExplanationPage.description:
A page of one value's explanation list, largest first, `explanation_entry_count_max` at a
time; the first page is what node detail carries.

entries.description: The entries of a gravity or unlocks list.

held.description:
The entries of a still-waiting list, which holds dependents rather than
contributions; empty for the other fields.

next.description: Where the next page starts, when there is one.

total.description: How many entries there are in all.

FixedBy.description:
What fixes an instant on a chain: a pin, an actual date, a date answer, or today (F1, F3,
F6). A chain always ends at one of these.

oneOf.description: A pin, which a resolution may move (F5).

An actual date, a fact that is never moved (F6): a recorded start or finish, or the
journey's `created_at`.
A date decision's answer, which a revised answer moves (A8).
Today, which holds unfinished work back: it starts, or finishes, no earlier (F3).

FixedDate.description: A date fixed on a chain.

Graph.description:
The graph document (resolved): nodes, roles, and kinds by key, every reference a key,
and, for a journey, its state (ARCHITECTURE, Engine > Model). Collections serialize
sorted by key, so a graph has one serialization.

default_owner.description: The role that owns nodes no ancestor gives an owner (A6).

insertions.description: The segment insertions the graph holds (B13).

retired_keys.description: Every key the graph has retired.

state.description: Journey state; empty for a route version or draft.

GraphId.description: Which graph a stored record belongs to (ARCHITECTURE, Schema outline: `graphs`).

GraphKey.description: The address of a record inside a graph, or of a whole node with everything on it.

oneOf.description: A node and everything attached to it.
A node's participation of one kind.
A note or link, with the node it is on when the address knows it.

GraphRecord.description: A record inside one graph: its content or, for a journey, its state.

oneOf.description: A node's participation of one kind.
An answer, with the rationale it was given with (B2).

rationale.description: Why it was given; none when the answer gave no reason.

oneOf.description: A tombstone: a removed route-copied node.

GroupState.description:
D1, C2: a group's display state, derived from its children and dependencies. Deprecated:
[`DisplayState`] (D8) is the state of every node, groups included; this stays, equal in
meaning on groups, until a later breaking release.

oneOf.description: It satisfies dependencies: its children and gates are done.
Its own or an inherited requirement, opening, or condition is not yet satisfied.
Open to start, nothing beneath it started.
Every relevant or undecided hard dependency satisfies dependencies.
A `requires_artifact` deliverable has an artifact link.
A `requires_note` deliverable or action has a note of its own (G4).
A placeholder has children or is atomic.

GuardFailure.description:
One specific guard failure (D4): what a bypass records, so a later distinct failure
still produces `stale`, and what `stale` lists.

oneOf.description: A dependency that does not satisfy dependencies.
No artifact link on a `requires_artifact` deliverable.
No note on a `requires_note` deliverable or action (G4).
A placeholder with no children that is not atomic.

Health.description:
`GET /healthz`: whether the server is serving. Answered 200 when it is, and 503 when its
store has failed closed and answers nothing until the process is restarted.

oneOf.description: The store has failed closed: every call errs until the process is restarted.

HeldDependent.description:
A dependent that completing a node would not yet free, and what else it waits on (C8,
Priority: Unlocks): one entry of node detail's `still_waiting`.

also_waits_on.description:
What else it waits on, besides the node: its unsatisfied requirements, condition
gates, and stage openings, each with how it arose. Never empty.

node.description: The direct dependent that stays held.

History.description: J4: a page of a journey's history, or of one node's, grouped by patch.

next.description: Pass as `after` for the next page.

patches.description: At most a page of events, grouped by patch, in log order; a large patch spans pages.

InsertedEdge.description:
An edge an insertion adds: `node` requires `requires`, one end in the segment and the
other in the graph (B13).

Insertion.description:
One placement of a segment version in a graph (PRD glossary, Insertion; B13). Its local
edits are not stored: they are its members' differences from the version it is on.

key.description: The key, minted by the client like any new key; unique in the graph.

kinds.description: Each segment participation kind beyond `owner`, likewise.

nodes.description:
Its members: each graph node it copied that the graph still holds, with that node's
key in the segment.

parent.description: Where it was inserted: the parent the root went under, or none for the top level.

roles.description: Each segment role, mapped to the graph role it became.

segment.description: The segment and the version the insertion is on.

InsertionKey.description: Starts with "i_"; at most id_bytes_max (64) bytes.

InsertionUse.description: One insertion of a segment version (C19).

upgrade_available.description: Whether the segment has a later published version.

Instant.description:
A point in time the date network solves for (ARCHITECTURE, Date network). A container's
entry is internal and never shown, so it has no form here.

oneOf.description:
A date decision's answer, a date rule's source (A8). It is the answered date, apart
from the decision's own instant, which is when it was decided (F2).

InstantPoint.description:
Which instant of a node (F2): work has a start and a finish; a decision or milestone has
one instant, which is both.

Journey.description: A journey domain: its fields, revision, and graph with state.

revision.description: The journey revision (H5).

JourneyHeader.description: A journey's own fields, apart from its graph.

created_on.description:
The deployment-local calendar day it was created, the `created_at` date rules
measure from (A8, A9). Stored beside the timestamp so the engine never converts time
zones.

lineage.description: The route version it follows, if any.

JourneyId.description: Starts with "j_"; at most id_bytes_max (64) bytes.

hits.description: Where the text was found, in order.

JourneyPage.description: A page of the journey index; `next` is where the next page starts, absent on the last.

next.description: Pass as `after` for the next page.

JourneyState.description:
A journey's state, on its graph document. Maps are keyed and sorted, so a state has one
serialization.

annotations.description:
Notes and links (G1): on each node, and on the journey itself, at most
`note_count_per_node_max` notes and `link_count_per_node_max` links.

local_edits.description:
Each route-copied node's local edits (B4), apart from its state so that an edit and
a transition on one node touch different records (H5).

pins.description:
Pins: explicit journey-level dates on nodes (PRD glossary, Pin). A pin from a
`feeds_milestone` answer is derived from the answer, not stored here (E3).

rationales.description:
The rationale each answer was given with, by decision (B2). A key here has an answer
beside it; an answer given without a reason has no entry, and reopening removes both.

role_fills.description:
Direct role fills, for roles without a filling decision (E3). A role with a filling
decision is filled from that decision's answer, which is derived, not stored here.

tombstones.description: Route-copied nodes the journey removed, so an upgrade does not re-add them (B4).

oneOf.description: Marked complete; still patchable, out of "mine" and cross-journey lists.
Archived: accepts only un-archiving or hard deletion.

latest_version.description: The latest version its route has published.

latest_version_node_count.description: The number of nodes in the latest published route version.

revision.description: Its revision.

upgrade_available.description: Whether its route has published a version newer than its own (C16).

Kept.description:
A journey's deviation from its route that an upgrade keeps, listed for the reviewer (B7:
locally edited and unchanged in the route).

oneOf.description: A marked edit on a route-copied node.
A participation kind the journey changed.
The graph's `default_owner`, which the journey changed.

KindChoice.description: What a segment participation kind becomes in the graph it is inserted into (B13).

oneOf.description: A new kind, minted from the insertion.

KindKey.description: Starts with "k_"; at most id_bytes_max (64) bytes.

LabeledChoice.description:
A choice with a label, as written. Unknown fields are an error, so a misspelled or
unsupported attribute is never silently dropped.

Level.description:
C2: one aggregation level of the canvas: the visible nodes for the shown kinds within the
drilled-in container, the edges re-targeted to visible stand-ins with duplicates collapsed,
and each container's roll-ups. Display only: stored state stays on each node.

collapsed.description: The containers collapsed that took effect: those within the level.

container.description: The drilled-in container; none for the whole journey.

display.description: The relevance classes shown; every class when absent.

edges.description: The edges, sorted by their ends.

nodes.description: The visible nodes, in tree order.

LevelDisplay.description:
C2: which nodes a level shows by how their relevance reads to a person. A node is
`relevant` when it applies; `conditional` when it may apply (its relevance is undecided,
or it is not relevant only because the decision it reads cannot be answered yet); and
`not_relevant` when it is settled as not applying (ruled out by an answer, a skip, or a
closed branch).

oneOf.description: May apply: undecided, or waiting on a decision that cannot be answered yet.

LevelEdge.description:
C2: an edge drawn at a level, between the nearest visible stand-ins of its ends, with the
edges it collapses.

from.description: The stand-in of the requirement side.

implicit.description: Every underlying edge is implicit (drawn dotted, C1).

to.description: The stand-in of the dependent side.

underlying.description: The edges it stands for, sorted; never empty.

LevelNode.description: C2: one visible node at a level.

display_state.description: D8: the state every surface shows for the node.

group_state.description: A group's display state. Deprecated: read `display_state`, which every node carries.

hidden_prerequisites.description:
Its hidden, unsatisfied prerequisites that no visible edge stands for: the "hidden
prerequisites" marker, which opens the trace (C7). Empty when it has none.

kept_work_pending.description:
A skipped container whose kept work is not yet done: "skipped, kept work pending"
(D1a).

parent.description:
Its nearest visible ancestor within the level, which it is drawn under; none at the
top level.

rolled_up.description:
The hidden nodes that roll up into it (a hidden action is a checklist item on its
deliverable, C4), in tree order.

Limit.description: A limit, by name (PRACTICES, Explicit limits).

Lineage.description:
A journey's link to the route version it was created from or last upgraded to
(PRD glossary, Lineage).

LinkedIdentity.description: One identity a user signs in with (ARCHITECTURE, Auth: users and identities).

provider.description: The provider, by its configured name.

subject.description: The provider's subject for the account.

verified_emails.description:
H3: the emails the provider marked verified at the last sign-in; only these match an
entity.

ListFlag.description: C9: a list filter that needs no argument.

ListPage.description: C9: a page of the list.

next.description: Where the next page starts, when there is one.

total.description: How many rows the query matches in all.

LocalEdit.description:
What a journey changed on a route-copied node (B4), so an upgrade leaves it alone. A
marker carries no reason (PRD glossary, Local edit).

oneOf.description: The node's explicit edge to the named requirement (added or removed).
The node's participation of a kind.

The node's kind or, for a decision, its answer type: what a replacement changes that
no single field edit can (B7).

Location.description:
Where a violation is (A15: listed by path; PRD Non-functional, Config-first: specific
enough to fix without reading source).

mutation.description: The mutation's position in the patch, when one mutation caused it.

path.description: The node's path in the graph the patch would produce.

LoggedEvent.description: An event and its position in the log, which orders history and pages it (J5).

seq.description: The position: increasing in commit order.

Markdown.description: Markdown, at most body_bytes_max (64 KiB) bytes.

decision.description: The decision whose answer is tested.
The decision whose answer is tested.

Mine.description: E4: the nodes the caller participates in.

entries.description: The nodes, in key order, each with the participation kinds the caller holds on it.

MineEntry.description: E4: a node the viewer participates in, with the kinds they hold.

kinds.description: The participation kinds the viewer holds on it.

MintedToken.description: A token just minted: the one time its secret is seen (H2).

agent.description: The agent the token acts as.

token.description: The bearer token; Cairn keeps only its digest.

Mutation.description:
One change within a patch (PRD glossary, Mutation), each emitting one event (J2). The
set covers every change the PRD defines; [`Mutation::change_class`] sorts each into
structural or state (PRD glossary, Structural change).

oneOf.description: Create the target journey, empty or from a route version (B1).

from.description: The route version to copy, or none for an empty journey.

oneOf.description: Hard-delete the journey and its events (A19).
Create the target route, with no versions and no draft.

kind.description: Process (the default) or segment; fixed from here on (A21).

oneOf.description: Retire the route (hide it from new-journey creation) or bring it back.
Publish the draft as the next version and clear it (A11).
Change one field of a node.

value.description: The field and its new value.

oneOf.description: Replace a node whole, as a kind or answer-type change does (B7).
Remove a node and everything its removal names (A18).
Change a role's id, title, or cardinality.

role.description: The role as it should be.

oneOf.description: Remove a role no participation or `fills_role` references (A18).
Change a participation kind's id, title, or cardinality.

kind.description: The kind as it should be.

oneOf.description: Remove a participation kind nothing references.
Set or clear the graph's `default_owner` role (A6).
Set a node's participation of one kind (E2, B5).
Remove a node's participation of one kind, restoring inheritance (E2).
Add a resource to a node (A10).

resource.description: The resource as it should be.

oneOf.description:
Insert a published segment version under a parent, wired to the graph's own nodes and
with its roles and kinds mapped, in one event (B13).

edges.description: The wiring: each edge joins one segment node and one node of the graph.

insertion.description: The insertion's key, new in the graph.

kinds.description: What each segment participation kind becomes, likewise.

omit.description: Segment nodes left out, each with its subtree.

parent.description: The group, deliverable, or action the root goes under; none for the top level.

roles.description:
What each segment role becomes; a role not named takes the graph's role with its
id and cardinality, else is added.

root_id.description: The root's id; the segment root's own, suffixed when a sibling has it, if none.

root_title.description: The root's title; the segment root's own if none.

segment.description: The segment and one of its published versions.

oneOf.description:
Answer or revise a decision (B2). The rationale belongs to this answer alone: a
revision that gives none leaves the decision without one.

rationale.description: Why it was given: markdown, free text under the body limit (B2).

oneOf.description: Edit a recorded start or finish date (F1, F2).
Fill a role without a filling decision (E3).
Pin a node's date (PRD glossary, Pin; F5 `repin`).
Move a pin by a number of days (F5 `shift`).

Snooze an actionable node, or a container (a group, or work with children) that has
work left beneath it, which holds every descendant off the acting frontier (B6).

until.description: Until a date or a node.

oneOf.description:
Lift a snooze (B6). A node held only through a container's snooze is refused, naming
the container to unsnooze instead.
Mark a placeholder atomic, or not (B10).

Move the journey to a newer version of its route, taking every clean outcome of the
three-way merge (route changes it did not edit, new nodes, orphans); conflict
resolutions and orphan removals ride after it in the same patch as ordinary mutations
(B7).

Link the journey to the version its saved route published (B9), in one event: the
lineage, each node the version holds route-copied and marked exactly where it differs,
every other node local, and the version's roles and kinds the journey lacks.
Change a node's provenance, as an upgrade orphaning it does (B7).
Set or clear a local-edit marker (B4: reset to route clears it).
Create an entity; may ride in any patch.
Change an entity's name or emails (deployment).

entity.description: The entity as it should be.

oneOf.description: Merge one entity into another (deployment, E6).

journeys.description:
Every journey referencing either, at the revision the merge was checked against;
at most `journey_count_per_merge_max`.

merged.description: The entity merged into it, whose key becomes an alias.

oneOf.description: Apply a proposal to its destination: its mutations follow its own revision check.

reviewed_revision.description: The proposal revision the user reviewed.

Mutations.description:
A journey's or route's mutations in one patch: at least one, at most
`mutation_count_per_patch_max`, in the order they apply.

Next.description:
C10: the acting frontier ordered, each item with its breadcrumb and why it ranks where it
does; when it is empty, what the journey waits on (C5, D5).

stalled.description: The stalled diagnostic, when the journey is stalled.

NodeDates.description: A node's derived dates (F3, F6). Every bound is null when nothing reaches it.

effective_date.description: A milestone's effective date (F1); none for other kinds, or when nothing gives one.

shortfall.description: The plan can no longer be met (F6).

slack_days.description: Latest start minus today; null is "no deadline".

NodeDerived.description:
Every D3 value for one node, with the inputs that explain it. The flags are D3's own,
each independent of the others, so they stay booleans rather than a state enum.

auto_reached.description: A pending auto-reach milestone that reads as reached (F1).

blocked_by.description:
What blocks it itself: its own explicit requirements, condition gates, and stage
opening, and its children, each unsatisfied. What it inherits is listed once, on the
ancestor that holds it (`blocked_through`), never copied onto each descendant. A node
that is not blocked lists what its own requirements, conditions, and opening still
hold back beneath it.

blocked_through.description:
The ancestors, nearest first, whose own unsatisfied requirements, openings, or
conditions block it through containment; each lists them in its own `blocked_by`.

display_state.description:
D8: the state every surface shows for the node, composed from relevance, stored state
and the flags beside it, which stay as they are.

max_child_gravity.description:
A container's largest child gravity, one level down.

Deprecated: read `subtree_gravity`, the gravity of the container's whole area. Kept so
existing clients keep reading it.

membership_lost.description: Its seeding entity left the role it was broken down by (B10).

needs_breakdown.description: A placeholder with no children that is not atomic (B10).

overdue.description: Non-terminal with its due before today.

rank.description: Rank, for nodes in the normalization set.

snoozed.description:
A snooze that holds over the node (B6): its own, else the one of the container it is
held through (`snoozed_via`).

snoozed_via.description:
The container whose snooze holds over the node (B6), the reason a descendant names.
Set even when the node's own snooze holds as well, so a node snoozed twice names its
container and shows its own target in `snoozed`.

stale.description: Why a terminal node's completing guards would now fail (D4).

subtree_gravity.description:
A container's subtree gravity (Priority): what rides on its whole area, the counted
weight of the container and its open descendants and everything downstream of any of
them, each once. Never less than any member's `gravity`; none for a node with no
children.

unassigned.description:
No owner (E1), for a non-group node that is in scope and unfinished; a not-relevant or
finished node, or a group, never is.

unlocks_from.description: The nodes completing this would unblock.

NodeDetail.description:
C8: one node in full. Its explanation lists (`derived.gravity_from`, `unlocks_from`)
carry their largest entries up to `explanation_entry_count_max` with their totals; the rest
page through the node's explanations endpoint.

annotations.description: The notes and links on it (G1), in key order.

answer_effects.description:
A decision's effects per choice (C12): what each answer brings in, drops, and leaves
to be decided later, with the role it fills and the milestone it pins.

children.description: Its children in key order, each with its state.

derived.description: Every derived value (D3) with what explains it.

local_edits.description: What the journey edited on it, for a route-copied node (B4).

node.description: The node: description, resources, participations as written, and its kind's payload.

rationale.description: The rationale the recorded answer was given with, markdown (B2).

record.description: Its stored state, provenance, and actual dates.

still_waiting.description:
The direct dependents completing it would not yet free, each with what else it waits
on (C8, Priority: Unlocks): the largest entries with the total; page the rest with
the explanations endpoint, field `still_waiting`.

oneOf.description: The weight; in a journey, a weight override (B5).

NodeFieldValueResolved.description: A new value for one node field.

oneOf.description: A new parent, or none to make the node a root.
A new weight, or none for the kind's default.

NodeKey.description: Starts with "n_"; at most id_bytes_max (64) bytes.

NodeKind.description: A node kind (PRD glossary: a fixed set).

NodeRow.description:
One node as a row of the list, the next list, or the snapshot (C9, C10, I3): what it is,
where it sits, and its derived signals.

ancestors.description: Its ancestors, root first: the breadcrumb (C10).

display_state.description: D8: the state every surface shows for the node.

overdue.description: Non-terminal with its due before today (D3).

rank.description: Its rank and terms, for nodes in the normalization set.

shortfall_days.description: Days the plan can no longer be met by (F6).

slack_days.description: Latest start minus today; none is no deadline.

snoozed.description: A snooze that holds over the node (B6): its own, else its container's.

snoozed_via.description: The container whose snooze holds over the node (B6).

stale.description: A terminal node whose completing guards would now fail (D4).

state.description:
Its stored state: what transitions act on. Prefer `display_state` for "what is its
status".

unlocks.description: Unlocks: the viewer's, in a ranking for them.

NodeState.description: One node's stored state in a journey.

atomic.description: A placeholder marked atomic, so it can complete without children (B10).

finished_on.description:
When the node finished: the actual date a milestone was reached (F1), the day a
decision was decided or work was done (F2).

skip_reason.description: Why the node was skipped, while it is (D1: a skip requires a reason).

started_on.description: When a deliverable or action was started (F2); editable like an actual date.

Notice.description: One advisory finding about a node of a route graph (A20).

message.description: A sentence for people, generated for display.

path.description: The node's path, to open it by.

NoticeCode.description: What a notice is about. One exists today; each later advisory finding adds a code.

oneOf.description:
A node with no chain to or from the graph's `final` milestone, so neither its priority
nor its dates feel that milestone.

OpenDecision.description: C18: an open decision and who owns it.

Override.description: An override to apply (PRD glossary, Override; Gating; D1a; D4).

oneOf.description: Exempt the node's subtree from an ancestor's skip.

Bypass guards on the node's transition in the same patch; the engine records the
specific failures present.

Overrides.description: A node's overrides (PRD glossary, Override): reasoned, logged departures.

bypass.description: A guard bypass on the node's transition (D4).

force_include.description: Treat the node as relevant despite conditions (Gating, Force include).

keep.description: Exempt the node and its subtree from an ancestor's skip (D1a).

ParticipationKind.description: A participation kind a graph declares beyond the built-in `owner` (A7).

id.description: The id, unique in the graph.

key.description: The stable key: optional in a file.

multi.description: Held by several entities rather than one.

oneOf.description: Map it to an existing role.
Map it to a new role.

ParticipationOrigin.description: Where a node's effective participation of one kind comes from (E2's order).

ParticipationRef.description: One participation, by node and kind.

anyOf.description: These entities; an empty list is an explicit "none".

deployment_revision.description:

id.description: The client-generated id that makes a resubmission safe (H5).

target.description: The domain or proposal it targets.

PatchAnswer.description: What an accepted patch answers (A17, H5, D7).

consequences.description: D7: what it newly caused, by journey; a journey with nothing new is left out.

notices.description:

receipt.description: The receipt: patch id, domain, content hash, and the revision produced.

oneOf.description:

PatchEvents.description: J4: one patch's events, in order.

PatchId.description: Starts with "p_"; at most id_bytes_max (64) bytes.

PatchReceipt.description:
What a committed patch id is answered from on resubmission (H5; ARCHITECTURE, Schema

content_hash.description: Its content hash: the same id with other content is rejected.

domain.description: The domain it was committed to.

revision.description: The revision it produced.

events carries (J1).

note.description: A note for each of its events.

patch.description: The patch; its target must be the path's domain.

PatchTarget.description: What a patch targets (A17): a domain, or a proposal within its destination domain.

oneOf.description: A proposal, by id, within its destination domain (I6).

Path.description: A node path: slash-joined ids from the root, at most containment_depth_max (16) segments.

Problem.description:
An error that is not a patch rejection: what went wrong, for a person to read, and the
request id the server logged it under.

error.description: What kind of error it is.

request_id.description: The request's id, as the server's logs name it.

ProblemCode.description:
The kinds of error that are not patch rejections (PRACTICES, Errors, panics, and
rejections). A rejected patch answers its `Rejection` instead.

oneOf.description:
The request is malformed: a body, path segment, or query parameter that does not
parse, or an unknown query parameter.
A body over the request size limit.
The patch's target is not the domain the path names, or is a proposal.

Cairn cannot draft the upgrade, save as route, or re-link asked for: the journey follows
no route, the version is not newer, or the draft is past a proposal's limits (B7, B8,
B9).

The journey moved since the page a cursor came from was read, so the cursor no longer
names a place in its order: start again from the first page.
Only a user may do this, not an agent acting for one (H2).
The process is at its in-flight request limit; retry after the `Retry-After` delay.
The process is at its SSE subscriber limit; retry after the `Retry-After` delay.
No store connection came free in time; retry after the `Retry-After` delay.

The request ran past the request duration limit. A patch may have committed:
resubmit it with the same patch id (H5).
The engine panicked: a bug. Nothing was committed.
The store or another part of the server failed.

created_by.description: The user it was created by or for.

destination.description: The domain it applies to, which may not exist yet.

proposing_agent.description: The agent that drafted it, if any (I6).

revision.description: Its editing revision, separate from the destination's (H5).

`POST /api/proposals/{id}/apply`: applies the proposal as the caller, its confirming user

note.description: A note for each of the apply's events (J1).

reviewed_revision.description: The proposal's editing revision the reviewer previewed.

`POST /api/{domain}/proposals`: a new proposal for the path's domain (which may not exist yet:
a proposal can create a journey or route at revision 0).

id.description:
The proposal's id, generated by the client (I6): a create resubmitted under it answers
the proposal its caller already holds rather than a second one.

ProposalDraft.description: A proposal's content: what creating or editing it carries.

base_revision.description: The proposal's editing revision the editor saw.

ProposalId.description: Starts with "pr_"; at most id_bytes_max (64) bytes.

ProposalPreview.description:
What a proposal would do to its destination now (C14, I6), for review: the items still
unresolved, and the candidate the resolved mutations produce, with every violation strict
validation finds in it.

consequences.description: For a journey, what the change does to derived state (D7).

frontier.description: For a journey, its frontier after, in rank order.

graph.description:
The destination's graph after: a journey's, or a route's draft. None when the
candidate is invalid, or for the deployment.

notices.description:
For a route's draft, the advisory notices of the graph after (A20); they never make
the proposal invalid.

unresolved.description: Items that still need a choice; the preview leaves their effect out.

violations.description: Every violation of the candidate; empty when the resolved proposal would apply.

ProposalReview.description:
`POST /api/proposals/{id}/preview` (C14, D7, I6): what applying the proposal now would do, and,
when its destination moved since it was drafted, what moved.

consequences.description:
D7, by journey: what applying it would newly cause; a journey with nothing new is left
out.

preview.description:
Its items still unresolved, the violations of its candidate, and for a journey the
graph and frontier after.

proposal.description: The proposal, at the editing revision a reviewer applies.

stale.description:
I6: present when the destination moved since drafting: applying it is stale until it
is refreshed and reviewed again.

base_revision.description: The proposal's editing revision the caller saw.
